title: Helm chart
description: Adds charts/cube, a production Helm chart adapted from gadsme's cube and cubestore charts: the API instances behind a Service with an optional Ingress, autoscaler and disruption budget, the refresh worker, and a Cube Store router and workers that list each other by stable name, as non-root, read-only pods that drain on shutdown and start only once they reach the data source and Cube Store and have compiled the model, with a NetworkPolicy around Cube Store, S3, GCS or volume storage, statsd-exporter metrics and a ServiceMonitor. values.schema.json rejects unknown keys and chart-owned variables; the chart:lint, chart:test and chart:docs tasks run helm lint with kubeconform, helm-unittest and helm-docs, pinned in mise.toml, and the check task runs the first two.

context_before: - `mise run check` passes before every pull request. When it reports that the SQL of a golden query changed, make sure the change is intended, then run `mise run check --update` and commit the snapshots with the change that caused them.
- A metric that a dashboard or an application depends on gets a golden query in `tests/queries`, with absolute date ranges.
added: - A change to the Helm chart in `charts/cube` comes with its unit tests in `charts/cube/tests` and a version bump in `Chart.yaml`. Each value is documented by the `# --` comment above it in `values.yaml`, which `mise run chart:docs` turns into the chart's README, and validated by `values.schema.json`.

context_before: `mise run image` builds the image every environment runs: Cube's own image with `cube/` copied into `/cube/conf`. Its tag is the Cube version followed by a hash of the data model, so one model always has one tag, and an unchanged model is never built, pushed or rolled out again. `mise run image --push` builds it for amd64 and arm64 and pushes it to `ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>`, or to the repository `CUBE_IMAGE` names.
added: `charts/cube` runs Cube in production on Kubernetes: the API instances behind a Service, the refresh worker and a Cube Store cluster, as non-root pods that drain on shutdown and take no traffic until they have compiled the model. [Its README](charts/cube/README.md) explains its design and lists its values. Before a pull request that changes it, `mise run chart:lint` lints it and validates what it renders for every environment, and `mise run chart:test` runs its unit tests; `mise run check` runs both before the data model check. After a change to `values.yaml`, `mise run chart:docs` regenerates its README.

description: Cube on Kubernetes for production, adapted from the community gadsme/cube and gadsme/cubestore charts. It runs the API instances, a refresh worker and a Cube Store cluster (router and workers), with graceful shutdown, non-root pods, a NetworkPolicy around Cube Store, autoscaling, disruption budgets and Prometheus metrics.
# Bump on every change to the chart; appVersion is the Cube release it runs.
| `api` | Deployment, Service, optional Ingress, HPA and PodDisruptionBudget | Cube's REST, GraphQL and SQL APIs. Scales out. |
| `worker` | Deployment, one replica | The refresh worker: builds pre-aggregations and refreshes caches. |
| `cubestore.router` | StatefulSet, one replica | Cube Store's metastore, cache and queue, and the entry point of queries. |
| `cubestore.workers` | StatefulSet behind a headless Service | Cube Store's query and build capacity, with stable names in `CUBESTORE_WORKERS`. |

The open-source Cube Store has no replication, so each Cube Store pod is a single point of failure. The chart pins the router to one replica and lists the workers by name, which is what Cube Store supports.

The pods run `image`. Build an image `FROM cubejs/cube` that copies the project's `cube.py` or `cube.js` and `model/` into `/cube/conf`, push it, and set `image.repository` and `image.tag`. The image is the unit of deployment: rolling out a model is rolling out a tag, and rolling it back is deploying the previous tag.

Cube reads its settings from environment variables. Plain ones go in `config.env`, a ConfigMap; credentials go in a Secret managed outside the chart and named by `config.existingSecret`, or in `config.secretEnv` on development clusters. The chart sets the variables that wire the pods together, which `config.env` cannot override: `values.schema.json` rejects them, along with any key the chart does not know. Changing `config.env` or `config.secretEnv` rolls the pods; for the external Secret, change `config.existingSecretRevision`.

The API and refresh worker count as started once `/readyz` reaches the data source and Cube Store and, given a `CUBEJS_API_SECRET` to sign a request with, the data model compiles, which also warms Cube's compile cache before the pod takes traffic. A rollout with a wrong connection or a model that does not compile therefore stops, with the error in the pod's events, and `helm upgrade --rollback-on-failure` returns to the previous release; an image without model files starts, so the chart can be installed before the first model. After that they are probed on their TCP port only, since `/readyz` and `/livez` fail with the data source: an outage would take every instance out of the Service, pre-aggregated queries included, or restart them all. On SIGTERM they drain for `config.gracefulShutdownSeconds` (`CUBEJS_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN`), after a five-second pause that lets the Service stop routing to them. Cube Store ignores SIGTERM, so its preStop hook sends SIGINT.

Cube Store keeps its data in `cubestore.remoteStorage`: an S3 or GCS bucket in production, separate from the bucket Cube exports from. The default, a PersistentVolumeClaim every Cube Store pod mounts, suits one Kubernetes node or ReadWriteMany storage. `cubestore.remoteStorage.s3.roleArn` assumes an IAM role through IRSA without keys.
